title: Choosing an overload by ability
description:
When several constrained templates could match, the compiler picks the **most constrained** one. That lets you write one function name with a different body for each kind of type.

Write three overloads of `std::string kind(const T& value)`:

| The argument is | Returns |
|---|---|
| an integral type (`std::integral`) | `"integer"` |
| a floating-point type (`std::floating_point`) | `"decimal"` |
| anything else | `"something else"` |

Then write a concept `Shape`: a type with `area()` returning something convertible to `double`, and `name()` returning something convertible to `std::string`. And a function `std::string describe(const Shape auto& shape)` returning for example `"square with area 4.000000"` (use `std::to_string` for the number).
